claims.text: Leads is a campaign objective you pick at campaign level in Meta Ads Manager. It replaces the old Lead generation objective, and you must also choose a conversion location, which decides where the lead is captured.

evidence.source_title: Create ad campaigns in Meta Ads Manager

claims.text: Leads is one of six objectives: Awareness, Traffic, Engagement, Leads, App promotion and Sales. It is listed as supported for image ads, and your objective determines which placements and calls to action you can use.

The conversion location is where the lead action happens. The Leads options include website, instant forms, calls, Messenger, Instagram, WhatsApp and app. Combined options also exist, such as website and instant forms.

evidence.source_title: Available conversion locations and events by objective in Meta Ads Manager

claims.text: The conversion event tells Meta which action you want people to take. Website offers events such as lead, complete registration and submit application. Website and instant forms uses Lead. Instant forms need no event. Not every location requires one.

evidence.source_title: Available conversion locations and events by objective in Meta Ads Manager

claims.text: Old Conversions campaigns map to Leads when the location is website or app. Old Messages campaigns map to Leads when the location is Messenger.

evidence.locator: Recreate a campaign that used an original ad objective in Ads Manager
evidence.source_title: How to choose an ad objective in Meta Ads Manager

claims.text: Use it when your goal is a form fill, sign-up, call or message enquiry rather than a purchase, and you can name where that action happens (instant form, website, call or messaging app).

evidence.source_title: Available conversion locations and events by objective in Meta Ads Manager

claims.text: Do not rely on it when you want sales or catalogue purchases. Those map to the Sales objective, and Traffic is the match for plain visits. Do not assume an old Conversions campaign maps to Leads, because it can also map to Engagement or Sales.

sections.summary: Meta documents the objective and conversion settings only. It does not give the full Ads Manager menu path, so this stops there.

claims.text: In Meta Ads Manager, start creating a campaign. At campaign level, select Leads as the objective.

evidence.locator: Campaign level in Meta Ads Manager
evidence.source_title: Create ad campaigns in Meta Ads Manager

claims.text: Choose the conversion location that matches where you want the lead captured, such as website, instant forms, calls or Messenger.

evidence.source_title: Available conversion locations and events by objective in Meta Ads Manager

claims.text: If your location requires a conversion event, choose the action you want, such as Lead for website and instant forms. Instant forms need no event.

evidence.source_title: Available conversion locations and events by objective in Meta Ads Manager

claims.text: Assess the website lead event you select, such as a lead or completed registration. Instant forms do not require you to choose a conversion event, so the measurement depends on where the lead is collected.

relationships.name: Leads objective
relationships.difference: Pinterest's Leads objective targets non-transactional outcomes such as sign-ups and leads. It replaces the legacy Conversions objective for non-transactional events, with CPM bidding. Meta does not describe Meta-style conversion locations for it.
relationships.context: Both cover lead and sign-up goals, but each sits in a different platform's objective structure.

relationships.name: Lead Generation objective (Search Ads)
relationships.difference: TikTok's Lead Generation is documented as an objective for its Search Ads campaign, where setup can start with Lead Generation and Search campaign pre-selected. It is not documented as a general objective across formats.
relationships.context: The goal is similar, but the scope is Search Ads, so don't treat it as a direct match for Meta's Leads.
